claim: Lipid droplets are lipid storage organelles found in nearly all cell types from adipocytes to cancer cells.
source: Lipid droplets are lipid storage organelles found in nearly all cell types from adipocytes to cancer cells.
evidence: This is a general statement about lipid droplets that draws from established scientific knowledge about their ubiquity across cell types.

claim: Current methods to study lipid droplets in vertebrate models rely on static imaging or the use of fluorescent dyes, limiting investigation of their rapid in vivo dynamics.
source: Although increasingly implicated in disease, current methods to study lipid droplets in vertebrate models rely on static imaging or the use of fluorescent dyes, limiting investigation of their rapid in vivo dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the limitations described in the manuscript and knowledge of existing methods.

claim: A lipid droplet transgenic reporter was created in whole animals and cell culture by fusing tdTOMATO to Perilipin-2 (PLIN2).
source: To address this, we created a lipid droplet transgenic reporter in whole animals and cell culture by fusing tdTOMATO to Perilipin-2 (PLIN2), a lipid droplet structural protein.
evidence: This is a primary finding directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Expression of the plin2-tdTomato transgene in transparent casper zebrafish enabled in vivo imaging of adipose depots responsive to nutrient deprivation and high-fat diet.
source: Expression of this transgene in transparent casper zebrafish enabled in vivo imaging of adipose depots responsive to nutrient deprivation and high-fat diet.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing imaging of adipose tissue under different dietary conditions.

claim: A large-scale in vitro chemical screen of 1280 compounds identified several novel regulators of lipolysis in adipocytes.
source: Simultaneously, we performed a large-scale in vitro chemical screen of 1280 compounds and identified several novel regulators of lipolysis in adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data from the LOPAC library screen described in the manuscript.

claim: The Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish line validated several novel regulators of lipolysis.
source: Using our Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish line, we validated several of these novel regulators and revealed an unexpected role for nitric oxide in modulating adipocyte lipid droplets.
evidence: This is supported by experimental validation data showing effects of compounds on adipose tissue in zebrafish.

claim: Nitric oxide has an unexpected role in modulating adipocyte lipid droplets.
source: Using our Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish line, we validated several of these novel regulators and revealed an unexpected role for nitric oxide in modulating adipocyte lipid droplets.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing effects of nitric oxide modulators on adipocyte lipid droplets.

claim: The nitric oxide pathway regulates lipid droplets in melanoma cancer cells.
source: Similarly, we expressed the PLIN2-tdTOMATO transgene in melanoma cells and found that the nitric oxide pathway also regulated lipid droplets in cancer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from ZMEL-LD cell line experiments.

claim: Lipid droplets are cellular organelles that act as storage sites for neutral lipids and are key regulators of cellular metabolism.
source: Lipid droplets are cellular organelles that act as storage sites for neutral lipids and are key regulators of cellular metabolism (Wilfling et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets are characterized by a monophospholipid membrane surrounding a hydrophobic lipid core.
source: Lipid droplets are present in most cell types and are characterized by a monophospholipid membrane surrounding a hydrophobic lipid core (Tauchi-Sato et al., 2002; Wilfling et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cells maintain energetic homeostasis and membrane formation through the regulated incorporation and release of fatty acids and lipid species from the lipid droplet core.
source: Cells maintain energetic homeostasis and membrane formation through the regulated incorporation and release of fatty acids and lipid species from the lipid droplet core (Kurat et al., 2009; Kuerschner et al., 2008; Fujimoto et al., 2007; Zimmermann et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets can sequester potentially toxic lipids and misfolded proteins during cellular stress.
source: Importantly, lipid droplets can assume various functions during cellular stress through the sequestration of potentially toxic lipids and misfolded proteins (Bailey et al., 2015; Listenberger et al., 2003; Vevea et al., 2015; Fei et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets maintain energy and redox homeostasis during cellular stress.
source: Importantly, lipid droplets can assume various functions during cellular stress through the sequestration of potentially toxic lipids and misfolded proteins (Bailey et al., 2015; Listenberger et al., 2003; Vevea et al., 2015; Fei et al., 2009), maintenance of energy and redox homeostasis (Liu et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets regulate fatty acid transfer to the mitochondria for β-oxidation.
source: regulation of fatty acid transfer to the mitochondria for β-oxidation (Rambold et al., 2015; Herms et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets maintain endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane homeostasis.
source: and the maintenance of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane homeostasis (Chitraju et al., 2017; Bosma et al., 2014; Velázquez et al., 2016; Vevea et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets actively participate in the innate immune response.
source: Moreover, a recent study demonstrated that lipid droplets actively participate in the innate immune response (Bosch et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Lipid droplets can be hijacked by infectious agents like hepatitis C virus to facilitate viral replication.
source: and, conversely, can be hijacked by infectious agents like hepatitis C virus to facilitate viral replication (Barba et al., 1997; Miyanari et al., 2007; Vieyres et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Lipid droplets can act as a storage pool in cancer cells after they take up lipids from extracellular sources, including adipocytes.
source: For example, lipid droplets can act as a storage pool in cancer cells after they take up lipids from extracellular sources, including adipocytes (Kuniyoshi et al., 2019; Nieman et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: White adipocytes contain a large unilocular lipid droplet.
source: White adipocytes, which contain a large unilocular lipid droplet, can be readily labeled by lipophilic dyes (Minchin and Rawls, 2017a; Fam et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and represents established knowledge about adipocyte structure.

claim: In vivo imaging of lipid droplets in adipocytes or other cell types is currently highly limited.
source: However, in vivo imaging of lipid droplets, in adipocytes or other cell types, is currently highly limited.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the limitations of existing methods described in the manuscript.

claim: The size of the lipid droplet can change very rapidly in response to fluctuating metabolic needs.
source: Understanding the dynamics of lipid droplets in vivo, rather than in fixed tissues, is important since the size of the lipid droplet can change very rapidly in response to fluctuating metabolic needs (Bosch et al., 2020; Fam et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In mice, much of adipose tissue imaging utilizes tissue fixation and sectioning, which can fail to preserve key aspects of the tissue structure.
source: In mice, much of adipose tissue imaging utilizes tissue fixation and sectioning, which can fail to preserve key aspects of the tissue structure (Berry et al., 2014; Xue et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Whole-mount imaging approaches in mice can be combined with adipocyte-specific promoters but still require tissue dissection and can be limited by tissue thickness.
source: Whole-mount imaging approaches in mice can be combined with adipocyte-specific promoters; however, these methods still require tissue dissection and can be limited by tissue thickness (Berry and Rodeheffer, 2013; Chi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Zebrafish offer a tractable model for high-throughput imaging of live animals.
source: Zebrafish offer a tractable model to address these limitations given the ease of high-throughput imaging of live animals.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: The casper zebrafish strain allows for detailed in vivo imaging without the need for fixation of the animal.
source: This is especially true with the availability of relatively transparent strains such as casper, which allows for detailed in vivo imaging without the need for fixation of the animal (White et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work describing the casper strain.

claim: Zebrafish adipose tissue is highly similar to mammalian white adipose tissue.
source: Although less well studied than other vertebrates, zebrafish adipose tissue is highly similar to mammalian white adipose tissue, and a detailed work has classified the timing, dynamics, and location of zebrafish adipose tissue development (Minchin and Rawls, 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Current imaging approaches using lipophilic fluorescent dyes or analogs in vivo can require extensive and repeated staining, which may restrict the ability to read out dynamic changes over time.
source: Current imaging approaches using lipophilic fluorescent dyes or analogs in vivo have advanced our understanding of lipid droplets in adipocytes and other cell types (Minchin and Rawls, 2017a; Minchin et al., 2018; Minchin and Rawls, 2017b; Carten et al., 2011; Farber et al., 2001; Otis and Farber, 2016); however, these methods can require extensive and repeated staining, which may restrict the ability to read out dynamic changes over time.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and inference about the limitations of existing methods.

claim: Fluorescent dyes such as BODIPY and NileRed have limitations in their specificity for the lipid droplet.
source: Furthermore, fluorescent dyes such as BODIPY and NileRed have limitations in their specificity for the lipid droplet (Daemen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: A probe-free imaging approach to study subcellular lipid populations is restricted to early-stage zebrafish.
source: Finally, although a probe-free imaging approach to study subcellular lipid populations has been recently described (Høgset et al., 2020), this method is restricted to early-stage zebrafish, which would fail to capture post-embryonic cell populations and tissues, including adipocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and inference about the limitations of the method.

claim: Transgenic lipid droplet reporters have been restricted to cell culture systems and invertebrate model organisms such as C. elegans and Drosophila.
source: To date, transgenic lipid droplet reporters have been restricted to cell culture systems and invertebrate model organisms such as Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) and Drosophila (Targett-Adams et al., 2003; Beller et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A similar approach to creating a lipid droplet reporter in zebrafish was recently described while this manuscript was in review.
source: although a similar approach in zebrafish was recently described while this manuscript was in review (Wilson et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to concurrent work.

claim: The -3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato reporter faithfully marks the lipid droplet.
source: We demonstrate that the -3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato reporter faithfully marks the lipid droplet, which enables robust in vivo imaging.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing colocalization with BODIPY and proper localization to lipid droplet membranes.

claim: The reporter can be applied to visualize adipocytes and to monitor adipose tissue remodeling in response to dietary and pharmacologic perturbations.
source: We show that this reporter can be applied to visualize adipocytes and to monitor adipose tissue remodeling in response to dietary and pharmacologic perturbations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from fasting, high-fat diet, and drug treatment experiments.

claim: Several novel pharmacologic regulators of adipocyte lipolysis were discovered, including nitric oxide.
source: Furthermore, we report the discovery of novel pharmacologic regulators of adipocyte lipolysis such as nitric oxide and demonstrate that several of these compounds can modulate adipose tissue area in our in vivo system.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the chemical screen and validation experiments.

claim: A zebrafish melanoma cell line (ZMEL) expressing -3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato (ZMEL-LD) was generated.
source: To facilitate the study of lipid droplets in novel contexts outside of adipocytes, we also generated a zebrafish melanoma cell line (ZMEL) (Heilmann et al., 2015) expressing -3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato (ZMEL-LD).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing the cell line creation and characterization.

claim: The ZMEL-LD cell line can be used to monitor changes in lipid droplet production in response to both known and novel regulators of lipolysis.
source: We confirm that this cell line can be used to monitor changes in lipid droplet production in response to both known and novel regulators of lipolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments in ZMEL-LD cells.

claim: PLIN2 is a well-known lipid droplet-associated protein that is ubiquitously expressed on lipid droplets across cell types.
source: We chose plin2 because it is a well-known lipid droplet-associated protein that is ubiquitously expressed on lipid droplets across cell types (Olzmann and Carvalho, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The adipocyte lipid droplet occupies the majority of space in the cell.
source: Since the adipocyte lipid droplet occupies the majority of space in the cell (Fujimoto et al., 2020), existing methods to visualize zebrafish adipocytes rely on lipophilic dyes and lipid analogs, which incorporate into the lipid droplet (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and represents established knowledge about adipocyte structure.

claim: In adult zebrafish, subcutaneous adipocytes reside proximally to the tail fin.
source: In adult zebrafish, subcutaneous adipocytes are known to reside proximally to the tail fin (Minchin and Rawls, 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression was detected in the zebrafish tail fin adipocytes and colocalized with BODIPY staining in 6-month-old adult Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish.
source: When we imaged 6-month-old adult Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish, we detected PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression in the zebrafish tail fin adipocytes, which colocalized with BODIPY staining (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: PLIN2 localizes to the lipid droplet membrane while BODIPY stains the lipid-rich core of the lipid droplet.
source: Lipophilic dyes such as BODIPY stain the lipid-rich core of the lipid droplet while lipid droplet resident proteins, such as PLIN2, localize to the lipid droplet membrane (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work and represents established knowledge.

claim: PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression was on the outside of the lipid droplet, whereas BODIPY staining was on the interior of each droplet in the adipocyte.
source: As expected, higher magnification images of tail adipocytes revealed that PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression was on the outside of the lipid droplet, whereas the BODIPY staining was on the interior of each droplet in the adipocyte (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Immunohistochemistry on the Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish tail fin showed that adipocytes express tdTOMATO.
source: Similarly, immunohistochemistry (IHC) on the Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish tail fin showed that adipocytes express tdTOMATO (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Visceral adipose tissue plays an important role in metabolism and participates in pathological processes of obesity, aging, and metabolic syndromes.
source: Visceral adipose tissue, otherwise known as abdominal fat, plays an important role in metabolism and participates in pathological processes of obesity, aging, and metabolic syndromes (Tchernof and Després, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In 21 dpf zebrafish, visceral adipose tissue is composed of abdominal and pancreatic visceral adipocytes predominantly located on the right flank near the swim bladder.
source: In 21 days post-fertilization (dpf) zebrafish, visceral adipose tissue is composed of abdominal and pancreatic visceral adipocytes predominantly located on the right flank near the swim bladder (Figure 2A; Minchin and Rawls, 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Visceral adipocytes visualized in brightfield demonstrate colocalization of PLIN2-tdTOMATO and BODIPY.
source: Visceral adipocytes visualized in brightfield demonstrate colocalization of PLIN2-tdTOMATO and BODIPY, as we observed for subcutaneous adipocytes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: IHC confirmed that the abdominal and visceral adipocytes of Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-Tomato) express tdTOMATO.
source: IHC confirmed that the abdominal and visceral adipocytes of Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-Tomato) express tdTOMATO (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Overexpression of perilipin proteins alters lipid accumulation in adipocytes.
source: Previous studies have shown that overexpression of perilipin proteins alters lipid accumulation in adipocytes (Sawada et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: No differences in visceral adipose tissue area were detected between Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish and their wild-type siblings using BODIPY staining.
source: Using BODIPY staining, we did not detect differences in visceral adipose tissue area (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: No difference in standard lengths was found between wild-type siblings and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) at 21 dpf.
source: Similarly, we found no difference in standard lengths between wild-type siblings and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) at 21 dpf (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No differences were detected between wild-type and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish when visceral adipose tissue area was normalized to standard length.
source: We normalized visceral adipose tissue area to standard length, similar to a Body Mass Index (BMI) in mammals, and did not detect differences between wild-type and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Similar development of the major adipose depots was observed between wild-type and Tg(-3.5:ubbplin2-tdTomato) zebrafish from 5 dpf larvae to adult fish.
source: Using BODIPY staining to visualize adipose tissue, we observed similar development of the major adipose depots between wild-type and Tg(-3.5:ubbplin2-tdTomato) zebrafish (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: The Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish faithfully recapitulates normal adipose tissue development.
source: Thus, the Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) zebrafish faithfully recapitulates normal adipose tissue development.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing no differences in adipose tissue development between transgenic and wild-type fish.

claim: Fasting induces lipolysis and leads to a reduction in the size of the adipocyte lipid droplet.
source: Fasting is a well-known mechanism for reducing adiposity, since it will induce lipolysis and lead to a reduction in the size of the adipocyte lipid droplet (Henne et al., 2018; Longo and Mattson, 2014; Rambold et al., 2015; Tang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A reduction in BODIPY-stained visceral adipose tissue was observed in both wild-type and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fasted zebrafish.
source: As expected, we observed a reduction in the BODIPY-stained visceral adipose tissue in both wild-type and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fasted zebrafish (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A significant reduction in adipose tissue area, standard length, and normalized area to standard length was measured between fed and fasted fish.
source: Similarly, we measured a significant reduction in adipose tissue area, standard length, and normalized area to standard length between fed and fasted fish (Figure 3C,D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C,D,E.

claim: No differences in adiposity or standard length were seen between wild-type and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish within the same diet.
source: Furthermore, we did not see differences in adiposity or standard length between wild-type and Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish within the same diet (Figure 3C,D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C,D,E.

claim: The transgenic expression of PLIN2-tdTOMATO reflects adipose tissue remodeling consistent with wild-type fish.
source: This suggests that the transgenic expression of PLIN2-tdTOMATO reflects adipose tissue remodeling consistent with wild-type fish.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing similar responses to fasting in transgenic and wild-type fish.

claim: An image analysis pipeline in MATLAB was developed to segment the visceral adipocytes in juvenile Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-Tomato) zebrafish.
source: To remove background fluorescence, we developed an image analysis pipeline in MATLAB to segment the visceral adipocytes in juvenile Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-Tomato) zebrafish (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a methodological development supported by the description and illustration in Figure 3F.

claim: An expected increase in adipose tissue area, standard length, and normalized area to standard length was seen over 7 days in fed Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish.
source: We saw the expected increase in adipose tissue area, standard length, and normalized area to standard length over 7 days in fed Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) fish (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H–J.

claim: The standard lengths for fasted fish were significantly lower than those for fed fish and remained stable over 7 days.
source: The standard lengths for fasted fish were significantly lower than those for fed fish and remained stable over 7 days, which we attribute to food restriction, disrupting zebrafish development (Figure 3I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Visceral adiposity was not reduced until after 2 days of fasting.
source: Notably, we found that visceral adiposity was not reduced until after 2 days of fasting (Figure 3H,J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H,J.

claim: Forskolin is a drug that induces lipolysis through cAMP signaling.
source: To achieve this, we used Forskolin, a drug that is known to induce lipolysis through cAMP signaling (Litosch et al., 1982).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: A reduction in both the adipose tissue area and normalized area to standard length was detected in Forskolin-treated fish, but no differences in standard length.
source: We detected a reduction in both the adipose tissue area and normalized area to standard length in the Forskolin-treated fish, but no differences in standard length (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Zebrafish have been used as a model for diet-induced obesity and share pathophysiological perturbations seen in mammals.
source: Zebrafish have been used as a model for diet-induced obesity and share pathophysiological perturbations seen in mammals, but few studies have focused on architectural changes of visceral adipose tissue (Chu et al., 2012; Landgraf et al., 2017; Oka et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: HFD-fed fish developed significantly increased visceral adiposity compared to fish fed with control feed after a week of HFD feeding.
source: After a week of HFD feeding, we observed that HFD-fed fish developed significantly increased visceral adiposity compared to the fish fed with control feed (Figure 4C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,E.

claim: Significantly greater visceral adiposity persisted after 2 weeks of HFD.
source: Although less dramatic between 7 and 14 days of HFD, we found that significantly greater visceral adiposity persisted after 2 weeks of HFD (Figure 4C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,E.

claim: No differences in the standard lengths of the control and HFD-fed fish were detected.
source: Interestingly, we did not detect differences in the standard lengths of the control and HFD-fed fish, suggesting that this formulation of HFD leads to specific enlargement of visceral adipose tissue (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: This formulation of HFD leads to specific enlargement of visceral adipose tissue.
source: Interestingly, we did not detect differences in the standard lengths of the control and HFD-fed fish, suggesting that this formulation of HFD leads to specific enlargement of visceral adipose tissue (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that HFD increased adiposity without affecting standard length.

claim: White adipose tissue is critical to lipid availability and cycles through lipolytic flux in response to energy demands.
source: As a major lipid depot for the body, white adipose tissue is critical to lipid availability and cycles through lipolytic flux in response to energy demands (Duncan et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In disease contexts such as cancer, adipocytes undergoing lipolysis act as a lipid source for neighboring cancer cells.
source: In disease contexts such as cancer, adipocytes undergoing lipolysis act as a lipid source for neighboring cancer cells (Lengyel et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Adipocyte-derived lipids have been directly shown to promote cancer progression in ovarian, breast, and melanoma cancer cells.
source: Adipocyte-derived lipids have been directly shown to promote cancer progression in ovarian (Nieman et al., 2011), breast (Balaban et al., 2017), and melanoma cancer cells (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: 3T3-L1 cells are the most commonly used cell line to study lipolysis in mammalian systems.
source: In mammalian systems, the most commonly used cell line to study lipolysis is 3T3-L1 cells, which can be differentiated in vitro to resemble adipocytes (Zebisch et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work and represents established knowledge.

claim: Atglistatin is an inhibitor of adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) that is the rate-limiting step of lipolysis.
source: As a positive control, we used Atglistatin, an inhibitor of adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) that is known to be the rate-limiting step of lipolysis and has been shown to inhibit lipolysis in cell lines and mouse models (Mayer et al., 2013; Schweiger et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Atglistatin potently inhibits lipolysis in 3T3-L1 adipocytes.
source: We confirmed that Atglistatin potently inhibits lipolysis in 3T3-L1 adipocytes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 29 out of 1280 compounds led to at least a 40% reduction in lipolysis as measured by glycerol release into the media.
source: Overall, we found 29 out of 1280 compounds that led to at least a 40% reduction in lipolysis as measured by glycerol release into the media.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the chemical screen.

claim: 2 of the top 10 hits from the screen (Auranofin and JS-K) modulated nitric oxide.
source: Looking more closely at the top 10 hits from this screen, we noted that 2 of the top 10 hits (Auranofin and JS-K) modulated nitric oxide (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Nitric oxide can be used for post-translational modification of proteins via S-nitrosylation.
source: Nitric oxide can be used for post-translational modification of proteins via S-nitrosylation (Stamler et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Increased nitric oxide has a suppressive role on lipolysis.
source: A previous study has shown that increased nitric oxide has a suppressive role on lipolysis, and Auranofin, a thioredoxin reductase inhibitor that promotes S-nitrosylation, can inhibit lipolysis in 3T3-L1 cells (Yamada et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Auranofin is a thioredoxin reductase inhibitor that promotes S-nitrosylation and can inhibit lipolysis in 3T3-L1 cells.
source: A previous study has shown that increased nitric oxide has a suppressive role on lipolysis, and Auranofin, a thioredoxin reductase inhibitor that promotes S-nitrosylation, can inhibit lipolysis in 3T3-L1 cells (Yamada et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: JS-K is a nitric oxide donor purported to promote S-nitrosylation.
source: Similarly, JS-K is a nitric oxide donor purported to promote S-nitrosylation, but it has not been shown to play a role in lipolysis (Nath et al., 2010; Shami et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: JS-K has not been shown to play a role in lipolysis prior to this study.
source: Similarly, JS-K is a nitric oxide donor purported to promote S-nitrosylation, but it has not been shown to play a role in lipolysis (Nath et al., 2010; Shami et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and inference about the novelty of the finding.

claim: Treatment of juvenile zebrafish for 24 hr with Atglistatin caused a significant increase in adipose tissue area without affecting standard length or fish viability at the maximally tolerated dose.
source: As expected, treatment of juvenile zebrafish for 24 hr with Atglistatin caused a significant increase in adipose tissue area without affecting standard length or fish viability at the maximally tolerated dose.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments in zebrafish.

claim: JS-K significantly increased adiposity in zebrafish.
source: Consistent with our screen results, we found that JS-K also significantly increased adiposity (Figure 5C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C,E.

claim: The effects of JS-K on adiposity were specific to the adipose tissue as standard length was not affected.
source: These effects were specific to the adipose tissue as standard length was not affected (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Modulators of nitric oxide can inhibit lipolysis in cell lines and lead to increased adiposity in vivo in zebrafish.
source: These data indicate that modulators of nitric oxide can inhibit lipolysis in cell lines and lead to increased adiposity in vivo in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of the in vitro screen and in vivo validation experiments.

claim: Upon uptake of adipocyte-derived lipids, cancer cells can store excess lipids in lipid droplets.
source: Upon uptake of adipocyte-derived lipids, cancer cells can store excess lipids in lipid droplets (Lengyel et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Accumulation of lipid droplets in melanoma cells has been associated with increased metastatic potential and worse clinical outcomes.
source: Accumulation of lipid droplets in melanoma cells has been associated with increased metastatic potential and worse clinical outcomes (Fujimoto et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: After a pulse of oleic acid for 24 hr, PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression was easily detected surrounding lipid droplets marked by MDH in ZMEL-LD cells.
source: We found that after a pulse of oleic acid for 24 hr, we could easily detect PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression surrounding lipid droplets marked by the lipid droplet dye Monodansylpentane (MDH) (Figure 6B, Video 1), similar to what we saw in the adipocytes (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Video 1.

claim: No difference in Lipidtox median fluorescence intensity (MFI) was found between ZMEL-GFP and ZMEL-LD cell lines after pulsing with increasing amounts of oleic acid.
source: Using the lipid droplet dye Lipidtox as a proxy for lipid droplet content, we pulsed the cells with increasing amounts of oleic acid and found no difference in Lipidtox median fluorescence intensity (MFI) between the two cell lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), indicating that the transgene was not having any unexpected effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression provided a much greater dynamic range than Lipidtox in reporting changes in lipid droplets of ZMEL-LD.
source: While both PLIN2-tdTOMATO and Lipidtox expression increased accordingly with oleic acid, PLIN2-tdTOMATO expression provided a much greater dynamic range (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–F), highlighting its advantages over standard lipid dyes like Lipidtox.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: Cells treated with Atglistatin and Auranofin demonstrated significantly higher lipid droplet-positive cells compared to cells with oleic acid pulse and DMSO.
source: In contrast, cells treated with Atglistatin and Auranofin demonstrated significantly higher lipid droplet-positive cells (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Cells given JS-K did not differ in the percent of lipid droplet-positive cells compared to cells with oleic acid pulse and DMSO.
source: Compared to cells with oleic acid pulse and DMSO, cells given JS-K did not differ in the percent of lipid droplet-positive cells (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Similar to adipocytes, ATGL is a key regulatory step in lipolysis in melanoma cells.
source: These data indicate that similar to adipocytes, ATGL is a key regulatory step in lipolysis in melanoma cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing Atglistatin's effect on lipid droplets in melanoma cells.

claim: Nitric oxide is a modulator of lipolysis in the melanoma context.
source: Moreover, we found that nitric oxide, which was identified in our adipocyte screen, is similarly a modulator of lipolysis in the melanoma context and can be utilized for future studies to target adipocyte-melanoma cell cross-talk.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing effects of nitric oxide modulators in melanoma cells.

claim: Changes in the lipid droplet content of a cell can occur in response to hypoxia, reactive oxygen stress, ER stress, and alterations in nutrient availability.
source: Changes in the lipid droplet content of a cell can occur in response to a variety of factors, including hypoxia, reactive oxygen stress, ER stress, and alterations in nutrient availability (Bailey et al., 2015; Bensaad et al., 2014; Chitraju et al., 2017; Velázquez et al., 2016; Vevea et al., 2015; Cabodevilla et al., 2013; Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: This is the first lipid droplet reporter in a vertebrate model organism.
source: To address such questions, we report the first lipid droplet reporter in a vertebrate model organism.
evidence: This claim is based on the novelty of the work, though a similar approach was described concurrently.

claim: The plin2-tdtomato reporter faithfully marks the lipid droplet in vivo.
source: We show that our plin2-tdtomato reporter faithfully marks the lipid droplet in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing colocalization and proper localization.

claim: A similar approach using knockin at the endogenous plin2 promoter was recently described while this manuscript was in review.
source: As a further validation of our approach, while our manuscript was in review, a similar approach using knockin at the endogenous plin2 promoter was recently described (Wilson et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to concurrent work.

claim: The Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) reporter can be used as an alternative to lipophilic fluorescent dyes to study adipose tissue across zebrafish developmental stages while preserving normal adipose tissue development.
source: We show that the Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) reporter can be used as an alternative to lipophilic fluorescent dyes to study adipose tissue across zebrafish developmental stages while preserving normal adipose tissue development.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing normal adipose tissue development in transgenic fish.

claim: The Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) line is sensitive enough to capture quantitative changes in visceral adipose tissue after short-term pharmacologic treatments with known regulators of adipocyte lipolysis.
source: We show that our Tg(-3.5ubb:plin2-tdTomato) line is sensitive enough to capture quantitative changes in visceral adipose tissue after short-term pharmacologic treatments with known regulators of adipocyte lipolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from drug treatment experiments.

claim: Differences in the kinetics of adipose tissue response to prolonged fasting and high-fat diet suggest a complex relationship between adipose tissue development and the nutritional and energetic requirements of the developing organism.
source: Differences in the kinetics of each response suggest a complex relationship between adipose tissue development and the nutritional and energetic requirements of the developing organism, which merits future investigation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental observations of different kinetics in response to dietary perturbations.

claim: Regulation of lipolysis by ATGL and nitric oxide pathways is conserved between adipocytes and melanoma cells.
source: We found that regulation of lipolysis by ATGL and nitric oxide pathways is conserved between adipocytes and melanoma cells although phenotypes downstream of nitric oxide may be cell type specific.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing effects of ATGL and nitric oxide modulators in both cell types.

claim: Phenotypes downstream of nitric oxide may be cell type specific.
source: We found that regulation of lipolysis by ATGL and nitric oxide pathways is conserved between adipocytes and melanoma cells although phenotypes downstream of nitric oxide may be cell type specific.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that different nitric oxide donors had different effects in adipocytes versus melanoma cells.
